title: The Last Spire Revisited
premise: Edmund Ravensworth, a runaway apprentice hiding in a valley where magic cannot follow, discovers the old gods are answering prayers again — and that her own forgotten bloodline is the reason. Dragged out of the valley by a disgraced knight and a god-touched child, she learns the king of Aldermarch has been hollowed out and replaced by a devouring spirit wearing his crown, sustained by stolen prayers. As the long winter falls, Edmund must choose between the anonymity she fled into and the dangerous identity she was born to, gathering a found family of outlaws, exiles, and one very tired god along the way. In the end she unbinds the true king at the cost of her own magic, exposes the usurping court to a justice older than law, and returns to the valley not as a fugitive but as its keeper.
about_author: Orsen Hartwell is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval petition letters before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people the histories forgot, from a drafty house full of rescued cats.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Years after fleeing her hedge-witch mistress, Edmund lives quietly in a valley where magic dies at the ridgeline, mending pots and lying low. When a dying stranger staggers in carrying a prayer-stone that still glows, the valley's silence cracks for the first time. Emotional beat: uneasy safety shattered; the past has found her.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered Wrong
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The stranger, Ser Maren, begs Edmund to carry the stone back over the ridge: prayers across Aldermarch are being answered, but cruelly, twisted. When Edmund touches it, she hears a voice call her by a name she buried. She refuses — until soldiers arrive hunting Maren. Emotional beat: denial giving way to flight.

chapters.title: Over the Ridge
chapters.summary: Edmund and Maren escape at night with the valley's other stray, Pip, an orphan girl who talks to things that aren't there. Crossing the ridgeline, magic floods back into Edmund like cold water, and she feels the old gods noticing her. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of becoming visible again.

chapters.title: The Hollow King's Road
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. On the road to the capital, Maren explains the truth: King Aldous stopped speaking eight months ago, and the queen regent rules through him. Pip's 'invisible friends' turn out to be minor gods, starving and frightened. Emotional beat: reluctant trust forming between three broken travelers.

chapters.title: The God of Small Doors
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. In a roadside shrine, a hearth-god offers shelter and warns Edmund: the thing on the throne eats gods, and it knows her mother's name. Edmund realizes her bloodline — god-speakers, hunted to near extinction — is why she can hear them. Emotional beat: identity as inheritance and threat.

chapters.title: Outlaws of the Ashwood
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Hunted again, the trio is saved by the Ashwood Company, outlaws led by Brannoc, a former royal guard who deserted when the king changed. Pip charms the camp; Edmund recognizes found family forming and flinches from it. Emotional beat: belonging offered, feared, half-accepted.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Brannoc recounts the night the king changed: a ritual in the chapel, the queen regent smiling, guards who spoke of it vanishing. He shows Edmund a scrap of the ritual's script — written in her mother's hand. Emotional beat: grief and fury; the conspiracy is personal.

chapters.title: The Mother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Decoding her mother's notes, Edmund learns the binding ritual requires a god-speaker's consent — freely given, long ago, by someone who believed they were saving the kingdom. Her mother didn't fail; she was deceived. Emotional beat: reframing shame as injustice.

chapters.title: Winter Comes Early
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The usurper's winter begins falling unnaturally fast, freezing villages whose prayers feed the crown-thing. The company shelters refugees; Pip's small gods begin winking out. Emotional beat: stakes made flesh — this is famine, not politics.

chapters.title: The Queen Regent's Mercy
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Captured and brought before Lady Vessia, the regent, Edmund expects cruelty and receives courtesy instead. Vessia claims the crown-thing ended a plague, a war, a famine — order at any price. She offers Edmund her mother's old place. Emotional beat: temptation of complicity.

chapters.title: Cells and Ciphers
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Imprisoned, the trio finds allies among palace servants — including the mute king himself, glimpsed through a grate, mouthing words only a god-speaker could read: 'Not dead. Buried.' Emotional beat: hope kindled in the darkest room.

chapters.title: Escape by Small Doors
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The starving hearth-god repays Edmund's earlier kindness, opening servant passages no one remembers. The escape costs Brannoc a wound that won't heal right — the crown-thing's touch lingers. Emotional beat: debts of care repaid; family chosen under fire.

chapters.title: The Dying God's Bargain
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The company reaches the last great god, Ysolde of the Long Night, who once governed winter itself. She reveals how to unbind the king: a god-speaker must stand where the bargain was struck and take the consent back — which will burn out their gift forever. Emotional beat: the price named aloud.

chapters.title: Ashwood Reckoning
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. A traitor in the company sells their route to Vessia's riders. Ambush in the snow; Edmund chooses to save Pip over seizing the ritual site while it stands open. Emotional beat: values tested — people over mission, and meaning it.

chapters.title: What Edmund Owes
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Convalescing in a refugee barn, Edmund finally tells Pip and Maren the truth of her apprenticeship: she ran because her mistress wanted to sell her gift to the crown. Pip says the obvious thing Edmund never believed: 'You're allowed to be loved anyway.' Emotional beat: shame released.

chapters.title: The Chapel Where It Was Struck
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The company infiltrates the capital during the Feast of First Snow. In the sealed chapel, Edmund reads the full bargain: her mother consented to save the dying king's life, never dreaming what would wear the opening. Emotional beat: understanding her mother at last — and forgiving her.

chapters.title: Vessia's Winter Court
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Confrontation with Vessia, who confesses she fed the crown-thing deliberately: a hollow king answered every crisis faster than a human one ever could. Maren, once her sworn shield, formally renounces her — justice spoken outside any courtroom. Emotional beat: accountability without mercy or cruelty.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At the bargain-stone, the crown-thing fights back with visions of every life order preserved. Edmund speaks the unbinding in her mother's voice, taking the consent back; the gift burns out of her like a brand lifted. The true king wakes screaming and free. Emotional beat: climax — sacrifice completed, selfhood reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Long Night Turns
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. With the crown-thing starved of stolen prayer, Ysolde reclaims winter and eases it. The waking king, frail and honest, opens his court to testimony — outlaw, servant, and god alike. Brannoc's wound heals as the old gods return. Emotional beat: dawn after the long dark.

chapters.title: Judgment Without a Throne
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Vessia, stripped of office, asks Edmund whether she'd have done differently with the same power. Edmund answers honestly: she doesn't know — which is exactly why no one should hold it alone. Justice lands as service and restitution, not execution. Emotional beat: hard-won moral clarity.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Offered a place at the new court, Edmund declines. She returns to the valley with Pip, Maren, and a convalescing Brannoc — magicless now, and lighter for it. The valley's silence feels like rest instead of hiding. Emotional beat: home redefined as people, not geography.

chapters.title: The Keeper of the Quiet Valley
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Edmund's POV. One year on: the valley takes in runaways and refugees; Pip's small gods visit over the ridge to say hello. A letter arrives bearing the restored king's seal — and Edmund, keeper of the quiet valley, reads it by firelight surrounded by family. Emotional beat: peace earned, identity chosen, story closed.
